audited_plan.image_description: A museum exhibit featuring a large Triceratops skull and partial skeletal mount in the foreground. The skull displays three horns (two brow, one nasal) and a massive solid frill. In the background, other dinosaur skeletons (including a hadrosaur) are visible in a gallery setting with windows and lighting fixtures.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows the characteristic three-horn arrangement of a Triceratops skull: two long brow horns curving forward/upward and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the bony rostral bone (beak base) is visible, the actual keratinous sheath/cutting edge is not preserved in this fossil specimen; only the underlying bone structure is present.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible limb bones (humerus, radius/ulna, femur) show the robust, columnar structure typical of quadrupedal ceratopsians, though full soft tissue is absent as this is a skeleton.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The massive parietal-squamosal frill is prominently displayed, extending well beyond the width of the braincase and facial region, consistent with Triceratops morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears as solid bone without fenestrations (openings), and marginal epoccipitals are visible along the edge, matching Triceratops characteristics.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a skeletal mount; no skin, scales, or soft tissue impressions are visible in the image. This feature cannot be assessed from bone alone.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mounted skeleton shows the characteristic ceratopsian posture with shorter forelimbs relative to hindlimbs, creating the expected dorsal slope.
The visible tail vertebrae are robust and relatively short compared to other dinosaur groups, consistent with ceratopsian anatomy.
